record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: connected CDH metric spaces and SLH
record.original_question: A separable space X is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if, for every two countable dense subsets D and E of X, there is a homeomorphism f from X onto X such that f[D] = E. A space is strongly locally homogeneous (SLH) if it has a basis B such that, whenever x and y lie in the same U in B, some autohomeomorphism of X sends x to y and is the identity outside U. Is every connected CDH metric space SLH?

evidence.quote: A separable space X is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if, given any two countable dense subsets D and E of X, there is a homeomorphism f : X → X such that f[D] = E.

Recall that a space X is strongly local ly homogeneous [34] if it has a basis B of open sets such that for every U ∈ B and every x, y ∈ U there is an autohomeomorphism h of X such that h(x) = y and h restricts to the identity on X \ U.
Problem 1. Is every connected CDH metric space SLH?
The problem was finally solved by van Mill [66].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a separable topological space X countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets D, E of X there exists a homeomorphism f : X → X with f(D) = E. Call a topological space X strongly locally homogeneous (SLH) if it has a basis B of open sets such that for every U ∈ B and every pair of points x, y ∈ U there is a homeomorphism h : X → X with h(x) = y and h(z) = z for all z ∈ X \ U.

Does there exist a connected, metrizable, countable dense homogeneous space that fails to be strongly locally homogeneous? Equivalently: is every connected CDH metric space necessarily SLH?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was resolved by J. van Mill, who constructed a connected CDH metric space that is not strongly locally homogeneous, giving a negative answer to the question. Related counterexamples (in weaker settings, e.g., a completely regular connected locally connected CDH space that is not SLH by Watson–Simon, and a connected CDH subset of the plane that is not SLH by Saltsman) are also recorded in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Topological Homogeneity – Arhangel'skii and van Mill
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of CDH spaces, SLH spaces, and constructions of connected CDH spaces that are not SLH.
status_evidence.claim: Van Mill solved the problem by exhibiting a connected CDH metric space that is not SLH.
